hidden_context: The user calls anydoc from a long-running Node.js API service (the backend of a contract-review product) through toMarkdownBytes.
The service runs as 6 replicas behind a load balancer, 1 GiB memory each. Redis is already part of the stack.
Local conversion is not the slow part. The slow documents are scanned PDF contracts that go through ocr: 'hosted': 8 to 20 seconds each, and billed per page.
About 35% of requests are repeats: the same document requested again by other users of the same tenant within days.
Document bytes come from object storage and never change after upload; each object already has a content hash.
The contracts are confidential. Cached output must be isolated per tenant, must be deleted when the tenant deletes the document, and must not sit in plaintext on local disk.
anydoc is upgraded monthly and its output changes between versions.
